purpose: Verapamil is used to treat high blood pressure, certain heart rhythm problems, and chest pain called angina. It can help your heart beat in a more regular, steady rhythm. Some forms are also used to prevent migraines.
how_it_works: Your heart and blood vessels use calcium to contract and squeeze. Verapamil blocks calcium from entering the heart muscle and blood vessel walls, which causes them to relax. This slows your heart rate, lowers your blood pressure, and makes it easier for your heart to do its job.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include constipation, dizziness, headache, feeling tired, and swelling in your ankles or feet. Some people feel nauseous or notice their heart beating more slowly. Constipation is very common, so drinking plenty of water and eating fiber can help.
warnings: Do not stop taking verapamil suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can be dangerous. Tell your doctor if you have liver problems, heart failure, or low blood pressure. This medication can interact with many other drugs, including statins, digoxin, and beta-blockers, so always share your full medication list with your pharmacist and doctor. Avoid grapefruit juice, as it can raise the level of this drug in your blood and increase side effects.
typical_dosing: Doses vary depending on what condition is being treated. A common starting dose for high blood pressure is 80 mg taken two to three times a day, or a long-acting version once daily. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on how you respond. Always take it exactly as prescribed and try to take it at the same time each day.
